intro.text: A region of Roshar that, in the time of the Silver Kingdoms, was split between Makabakam and Valhav.
A small nation in southern Roshar between Jah Keved and Tu Fallia, with mountains to the north and the Tarat Sea to the south.

description.text: One river divides the country in half. Its coastline is long, yet it has no port or settlement of wider note.

Squeezed between northern mountains and the southern coast, Triax is a bottleneck for any army crossing southern Roshar, which makes moving troops through it hard and gives the advantage to whoever defends it.
The land is lush compared with eastern nations like Alethkar, thick with grasses and vines, and home to animals such as a tentacled creature with leathery skin instead of chitin.
People live in small villages, often in forest clearings, in houses raised on stilts though floods are rare. Buildings are often overgrown with the same vines that cover the land.
Many villagers carry tools that are not made of metal.

items.text: People live in small villages, often in forest clearings, in houses raised on stilts though floods are rare. Buildings are often overgrown with the same vines that cover the land.
Many villagers carry tools that are not made of metal.

The Veden king NanHar invaded the area but died during the war. His brother and successor, NanKhet, died within three months, and the Siln dynasty took the Veden throne. Whether the conquest succeeded is unknown.
Vstim bought wormy grain cheaply in Triax, knowing he could sell it at a profit elsewhere.

Contact with Triax, spanreeds included, was lost only weeks after the Everstorm arrived. It remained under the control of Odium's forces after the Battle of Thaylen Field, so the coalition supplied its troops in Emul by sea on Thaylen ships instead of going through Triax.

told.title: Split between two kingdoms
told.text: In the age of the Silver Kingdoms, this land was divided in half, part of it in Makabakam and part in Valhav.

told.title: Desolation after Desolation
told.text: Again and again the Desolations threw the people here back to stone tools. Each time the Heralds returned, they helped them rebuild, often as far as the age of bronze, with the Herald Kalak among those who helped.

told.title: NanHar's invasion
told.text: At some point the Veden king NanHar invaded the area, but he died in the war. His brother NanKhet, who followed him, died within three months, and the Siln dynasty took the Veden throne. Whether the Veden conquest of Triax succeeded is unknown.

told.title: Out of the way
told.text: Some trade still passed through Triax: Vstim bought its wormy grain cheaply, knowing he could sell it at a profit in other lands. Dalinar never knew the land first-hand.

told.title: Cut off by the enemy
told.text: When the Everstorm came, Odium's forces gathered in Marat and struck fast along the coast of the Tarat Sea, Triax included. Within weeks all contact with Triax, spanreeds included, was lost.

told.title: Held by the enemy
told.text: After the Battle of Thaylen Field, Triax stayed under Odium's control. Once Queen Fen won a decisive victory at sea, the coalition ruled the southern waters and used Thaylen ships to supply its troops in Emul, never needing to march through Triax.
